newsitem.title: USA: Conn. still analyzing options for cutting budget.
newsitem.headline: Conn. still analyzing options for cutting budget.

text.p: Connecticut's Gov Rowland Administration is continuing to analyze options for trimming how much state agencies spend by as much as 10 percent in some cases, a spokesman for the state budget said on Tuesday.

He explained that Gov. John Rowland in early August asked the agencies to come up with specific proposals, which might include downsizing or privatizing, and the agencies started turning in their plans in October.
Since then the Administration has been studying the proposals but it does not expect to release specific details until the budget in completed sometime in February.

The Connecticut Conference of Municipalities, a nonprofit, civic association, in late November released the following detailed list of proposed cuts, which the spokesman for the state budget division could not confirm.
--slashing around $150 million from the State Board of Education.
--snipping about $4.2 million from the Department of Public Safety.
--trimming more than $5.0 million from the Department of Children and Families.
--paring the Department of Motor Vehicles by $2.2 million.
--trimming more than $7.5 million from the Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services.
--cutting more than $260 million from the Department of Social Services.
--reducing over $4 million from the Department of Environmental Protection.
--cutting around $14 million from the Office of Policy and Mangement, and about $6.5 million from intergovernmental programs.
--paring about $1.7 million from the budget for the Department of Economic and Community Development.
--trimming about $5.5 million from the Department of Public Health.
--cutting teachers' retirement by almost $19 million.
--slashing the Department of Transportation by around $29 million. The plan includes continuing to pay for bridge maintenance with bonding instead of pay-as-you-go.
--cutting nearly $40 million from the Department of Corrections.
--slicing up to $43 million from the Deptartment of Metnal Retardation.
--paring the Connecticut State University by as much as around $8.5 million.
--trimming the Department of Labor by around $1.6 million.
